name: Raúl Reyes

name: Chantal Akerman
milestone_by_age_26: Made her first short film 'Saute ma ville' at age 18 in 1968, which premiered at the International Short Film Festival Oberhausen in 1971.
early_history_summary: Inspired by Godard's Pierrot le fou at age 15, Akerman entered a Belgian film school at 18 but dropped out during her first term to make her first short film, Saute ma ville, funding it by trading diamond shares on the Antwerp stock exchange. The film premiered at Oberhausen in 1971, launching her career.
family_context_summary: Born to Polish-Jewish Holocaust survivor parents in Brussels; family ran a small leather goods shop and led a working-class life. Mother survived Auschwitz and was exceptionally close to Chantal.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in film or arts; parents ran a small leather goods shop in Brussels.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Holocaust survivor family, working-class, self-funded film, dropped out of school
evidence_summary: Chantal Akerman was born to Polish-Jewish Holocaust survivors in Brussels who ran a small leather goods shop. Inspired by Godard at 15, she entered film school at 18 but immediately dropped out to make Saute ma ville, self-funding it through diamond share trading. The film premiered at Oberhausen in 1971, establishing her as a distinctive avant-garde voice. Her mother's Holocaust trauma and the family's working-class immigrant background profoundly shaped her artistic vision and drive.
starting_point: Born to Polish-Jewish Holocaust survivor parents in Brussels; family ran a small leather goods shop and lived a working-class life.
current_position: Died October 5, 2015 in Paris at age 65; final role as filmmaker and film professor at City College of New York (2011-2015).

trajectory.event: Made first short film Saute ma ville after dropping out of Belgian film school, self-funding it through diamond share trading.

Directed Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles, later ranked the greatest film of all time by Sight & Sound in 2022.
Appointed as film professor at the City College of New York.
Died in Paris on October 5, 2015.

name: Robert Zemeckis
milestone_by_age_26: Won a Student Academy Award (Special Jury Prize) for his short film 'A Field of Honor' at USC in 1973, which caught the attention of Steven Spielberg.
early_history_summary: Raised in a working-class family on Chicago's South Side with no exposure to arts, Zemeckis began making films with an 8mm camera in high school. He transferred to USC's School of Cinematic Arts, where he made the award-winning short A Field of Honor and met his writing partner Bob Gale. Spielberg noticed his student work and helped launch his professional career.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class Italian-Lithuanian American family on Chicago's South Side; father was a car mechanic, mother a homemaker. No art, music, or books in the household; television was the only inspirational medium.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in film or arts; father was a mechanic. The family had no cultural exposure to the arts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: USC film school, Spielberg mentorship, Hollywood proximity, Bob Gale partnership
evidence_summary: Robert Zemeckis grew up in a working-class Chicago family with no arts exposure, finding inspiration only in television. He began making 8mm films in high school and transferred to USC's elite School of Cinematic Arts in Los Angeles, where he won a Student Academy Award for A Field of Honor at 21. Spielberg noticed the film and helped Zemeckis and writing partner Bob Gale secure their first professional deals. The combination of USC's film program, proximity to Hollywood, and Spielberg's mentorship were critical institutional advantages.
starting_point: Born to a working-class Italian-Lithuanian American family on Chicago's South Side; father was a car mechanic, no art or books in the household.

He joined the Italian national ski team in 1970 and made his World Cup debut in December 1972, winning his first two races and becoming the youngest male World Cup winner ever.

name: Jan Szczepański
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Polish national amateur boxing championship as a lightweight in 1961 at age 21, and repeated as national champion in 1962 and 1963.
early_history_summary: Born to a peasant family in Małecz, Poland, Szczepański was introduced to boxing by a school teacher in Zduńska Wola. He trained at local clubs before joining Legia Warszawa in 1960 as a military boxer, where he won Polish national titles from 1961-63. His career was then interrupted by a heart arrhythmia diagnosis and personal struggles before a remarkable comeback leading to European and Olympic gold.
family_context_summary: Born to a peasant family in the village of Małecz near Tomaszów Mazowiecki, Poland; parents were Wincenty and Helena. Grew up in poverty in post-war Poland.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in boxing; a school teacher (Tomasz Lasota) first put boxing gloves on him at the mechanical technical school in Zduńska Wola.

A school teacher introduced him to boxing at the mechanical technical school, and he progressed through local clubs to Legia Warszawa, the military sports club, where he won Polish national titles from 1961-63 at ages 21-23. His career was then halted by a heart arrhythmia diagnosis and personal struggles including alcoholism, before a remarkable comeback to win European and Olympic gold. His peasant origins and the hardships he faced created a powerful urgency that drove his boxing career.

current_position: Died January 15, 2017 in Warsaw at age 77; final role as Olympic boxing gold medalist and boxing coach.

name: Kurt Cobain
milestone_by_age_26: Released Nirvana's second album 'Nevermind' on DGC Records in September 1991 at age 24, which topped the Billboard charts and became a global cultural phenomenon.
early_history_summary: Born in Aberdeen, Washington to a waitress and a car mechanic, Cobain's parents divorced when he was 8, leading to a turbulent childhood shuffled between relatives. He received a guitar at 14, discovered punk rock through the Melvins' Buzz Osbourne, and formed Nirvana with Krist Novoselic in 1987 at age 20. After releasing the debut album Bleach on Sub Pop in 1989, Nirvana signed with DGC and released Nevermind in 1991, catapulting them to global fame.
family_context_summary: Born in Aberdeen, Washington to a waitress mother and car mechanic father; working-class family in a depressed logging town. Parents divorced when he was 8, leading to a fractured childhood being shuffled among relatives.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in music; aunt Mari Earl gave him an old guitar and his uncle Chuck Fradenburg gave him a used electric guitar at 14. No sustained musical mentorship in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Broken home, Pacific Northwest grunge scene, Sub Pop, punk rock immersion, working-class
evidence_summary: Kurt Cobain was born to a working-class family in Aberdeen, Washington, a depressed logging town. His parents' divorce when he was 8 created a turbulent, displaced childhood that deeply shaped his angsty songwriting. He received a guitar at 14 and found his artistic direction through the Pacific Northwest punk rock scene, particularly the Melvins. The Seattle/Pacific Northwest grunge movement of the late 1980s provided the structural wave, and Sub Pop's indie label infrastructure gave early distribution. His broken home and outsider status were clearly catalytic to his artistic voice, while his partnership with Krist Novoselic provided the complementary team that became Nirvana.
starting_point: Born in Aberdeen, Washington to a waitress mother and car mechanic father; working-class family in a depressed logging town; parents divorced when he was 8.
current_position: Died c. April 5, 1994 in Seattle at age 27; final role as lead vocalist, guitarist, and primary songwriter of Nirvana.

trajectory.event: Formed Nirvana with Krist Novoselic in the Aberdeen/Aberdeen area of Washington state.

Married Courtney Love; daughter Frances Bean Cobain was born.
Released In Utero, Nirvana's final studio album, to critical acclaim.
Died by suicide at his Seattle home on approximately April 5, 1994.
